items.text: WHERE IS SHE? Alison Hammond's absence explained as This Morning presenter rushes out of studio
items.article: Alison Hammond left Friday's This Morning during a pet phone-in, with Dermot O'Leary later explaining her absence. This Morning presenter Dermot O'Leary has addressed his co-star Alison Hammond 's sudden absence from the show. The duo were hosting Friday's programme as usual, while Ben Shephard and Cat Deeley present the rest of the week. However, over an hour into the programme, Alison left, leaving Dermot presenting alone. During a phone-in from pet owners with Dr Scott, there appeared to be problems in the studio, as the camera caught Dermot helping Alison out of the studio, while Dr Scott looked concerned. Dermot later explained her absence, saying she wouldn't be returning to the show on Friday, October 2. He had first said, after a break: "Welcome back to This Morning , Alison is feeling a little unwell, so she's just had to duck out. Hopefully she'll be back." He later confirmed: "Ali's feeling a little unwell so I'll be here for the rest of the show," reports the Mirror . Viewers took to social media to express their concerns for the beloved presenter. One person wrote: "Hope Alison Is ok and its nothing more than a bit unwell." Another said: "Plenty of people there to care for Alison. Get well soon lovely x." items.article: FOR the millions of Brits with ADHD, a daily stimulant tablet holds the potential to unlock a new world - one that is quieter, less chaotic, with a... FOR the millions of Brits with ADHD, a daily stimulant tablet holds the potential to unlock a new world – one that is quieter, less chaotic, with a level playing field. The surge in prescription drugs for ADHD has been explosive in the past few years. But for some, it’s not all it’s cracked up to be. Others are spooked by little-known risks on the heart and even death, leaving them searching more desperately for answers to manage symptoms. When Michelle Akpata, 30, was diagnosed with ADHD, she hoped a prescription from her GP would rid her of the extra load she’d been carrying for years. “It often felt like running a marathon mentally just to stay organised throughout the day,” says Michelle, a broadcaster and radio presenter from London . “I realised that my difficulty maintaining focus and structure wasn’t just stress, but a consistent pattern affecting my day-to-day life.” But after starting Ritalin (10mg), the initial surge in energy gave way to troubling side effects.

items.key: ai:a man found $128k on top of a bank of america atm. here's what he did next
items.text: A man found $128K on top of a Bank of America ATM. Here's what he did next
items.article: A Texas man found a bag containing $128,514 on top of a Bank of America ATM on Aug. 3. Here's what he did next. A bag of cash sitting on top of a Bank of America ATM put a Texas man in a peculiar situation. While many would have kept the money, he searched for the rightful owner. The 37-year-old Lewisville man found the bag at about 10 a.m. on Aug. 3 at a Bank of America ATM in the Texas city about 30 miles north of Dallas. A second bag containing 19 checks was also at the scene, according to CBS News Texas and NBC 5 , both citing Lewisville police. The man, whose name hasn't been publicly confirmed but who local outlets reported works as a barber, was at the ATM with a 42-year-old woman when they spotted the bags. Information on one of the bags appeared to link the money to a nearby Chick-fil-A, so he drove to the restaurant to try to return it. After a manager told the man the cash didn't belong at the location, he called 911, and officers responded to secure the bags and determine who owned them, NBC 5 reported. USA TODAY contacted Lewisville police and Bank of America on Oct. 1, but has not received a response. Inside the cash bag was a bank receipt showing how much money it was supposed to contain. Police counted the cash twice and used a digital currency counter to verify the total, according to CBS News.

items.text: As Texas declares state of emergency over fuel shortage, what's dyed diesel?
items.article: As global oil supplies continue to tighten up amid ongoing geopolitical conflicts that have pushed up fuel prices, the governor of Texas has declared a state of emergency. If you get Global News from Instagram or Facebook - that will be changing. Find out how you can still connect with us . As global oil supplies continue to tighten and fuel prices soar , the governor of Texas declared a state of emergency over a shortage of diesel fuel. Declaring a state of emergency can unlock a government’s ability to temporarily modify certain policies in order to protect the general public: in the case of Texas, this includes waiving restrictions on what’s known as dyed diesel. Governor Greg Abbott of Texas issued an emergency notice on Monday. “The shortage of diesel fuel poses an imminent threat or occurrence of harm to the public health and safety in the State of Texas,” the notice says. “A shortage of diesel fuel will impose harmful effects upon the agriculture and ranching industries by increasing the price per acre to achieve similar yields, reducing investment in farm and ranch machinery, and driving up supply chain expenses.”

items.key: ai:your health insurance premiums may take a big jump in 2027 — here's why
items.text: Your health insurance premiums may take a big jump in 2027 — here’s why
items.article: Many consumers are likely on the hook for an increase of about 10% or more in 2027, experts said. Many consumers face much higher health insurance premiums and cost-sharing next year, as factors like increased use of GLP-1 drugs , the expiration of enhanced Obamacare subsidies and a high U.S. inflation rate push up costs across the healthcare system, experts said. The dynamic is stressing household budgets at a time when they're already strained by broader affordability issues , a key issue in the upcoming midterm elections. "They can expect to pay more," said Jonathan Oberlander, a professor of health policy and political science at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. "Not just in terms of premiums — but also in terms of deductibles and copayments." Most Americans under age 65 — about 166 million people — get health insurance via employer-sponsored health plans. Employers generally subsidize the cost of health insurance for their workers by covering a large portion of their monthly premium payments. The average worker paid $6,850 of annual premiums in 2025, while employers contributed more than $20,000 per worker, according to KFF, a health policy research group. In 2027, the cost for employers to provide health benefits will rise by an estimated 8.2% per worker, on average — the largest increase since 2003, even after accounting for cost-reduction measures by employers, according to Marsh, a consulting firm.

items.text: How familial DNA led to conviction in Arizona woman’s violent murder
items.article: Allison Feldman, a 31-year-old resident of Scottsdale, Arizona, was found dead in her home in 2015. Allison Feldman was found dead in her Scottsdale home in 2015. Allison Feldman returned to her Arizona home after running errands on a typical Tuesday on Feb. 17, 2015. But when the 31-year-old's family and boyfriend did not hear from her later that evening into the following day, they knew something was wrong. "We talked almost every day," her father, Harley Feldman, told local ABC affiliate reporters. "My wife said, it's just not right, things were out of normal." Concerned for his daughter, Harley called Scottsdale Police for a welfare check on her. At the same time, unbeknownst to Harley, Feldman's boyfriend, Alex Stone, went to her house in Scottsdale and found her dead on the floor, naked and bloodied. The hunt for Feldman's killer proceeded for three years until investigators employed a forensic tool never before used in the state's history. But the battle to use that DNA match went on for several more years.

items.key: ai:why james acaster could be this year's best traitor
items.text: Why James Acaster could be this year's best Traitor
items.article: Does trustworthy Amol Rajan have what it takes to lie and betray? Or will Acaster's nervy energy and unpredictability earn his survival? The Celebrity Traitors is the best gig in British broadcasting . Everyone wants to have a go, as is obvious from the second series’ ridiculously good cast, but something that is easily forgotten in the five – yes, five – months of excitement since it was announced is how quickly it can be over, no matter how much of a “big dog” you are. It is the best gig in British broadcasting, but also the most brutal – where you may not last more than an episode and disappointment, vulnerability and resentment loom. Even the stars can come away feeling short-changed. And so, we ended the very first episode with a savage cliffhanger: one of the two biggest bookings are getting the chop. In the dead of night, Amol Rajan , the ubiquitous broadcaster who just left the Today programme , was summoned to the old stone chapel where he stood, shivering in a shearling jacket in honour of his beloved Del Boy, to meet the Traitors face-to-face and plead for his salvation. Next to him, heart also sinking, was an uneasy James Acaster , one of the most accomplished stand-ups of his generation. Both men wound up lying in coffins awaiting their fate. One will be given a Traitors cloak; the other will have a coffin lid slammed in their face. I’m gutted it’s already down to those two, who I’d love to see stay in the game for weeks, but they brought it on themselves.

items.key: ai:flattering haircuts for women over 60
items.text: Flattering haircuts for women over 60
items.article: From mid-length styles to glossy shine and ultra-long hair, these are the celebrity inspired haircuts perfect for women over 60 One look at recent red carpets and runway shows and it's clear the era of women in midlife feeling they have to cut their hair short is well and truly over. From Sarah Jessica Parker's waist-length hair to Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock's long locks in Practical Magic 2 , our A-listers are proving there's no rule when it comes to hair in midlife and beyond. To inspire your next salon appointment, we spoke to celebrity stylist and owner of Soho's Salon 64 , Ricky Walters, for his take on the most flattering haircuts for midlife women. While long hair is all the rage for A-listers, it's not the most practical for us mere mortals, which is why mid-length manes are the go-to for many of us. "Very long, heavy hair can sometimes feel ageing, but equally, an overly structured, 'strict history teacher' bob can have the same effect. On the other hand, mid-length hair is almost always a wonderfully flattering choice for a more mature woman," Ricky says. On the beauty of a mid-length cut, Ricky says it strikes the perfect balance of polished and sophisticated, but still youthful and effortless. "Soft, gentle layering, particularly around the face, is key, as it creates movement and softness rather than making the style feel too severe," he says.
